text:
maria: Hey all, quick onboarding question. I'm testing streaming completions from my laptop with my hosted API key and after ~10s I get a burst of 429s and the stream closes. Is this expected for dev usage?

devx: Welcome! :wave: For local dev we recommend using the sandbox key or routing through the dev-proxy. Hosted keys are treated as production and are subject to stricter per-second and per-IP limits.

maria: Sandbox key helped but it's still flaky for long-running streams. Any config I should check?

devx: Two things to try: 1) enable keepalive on the client and dev-proxy to avoid reconnect storms; 2) reduce chunk size / token window if you can. Sometimes clients that do very frequent small reads end up hitting internal token-burst buckets.

andy: Also watch for per-IP throttles. If you have other teammates on the same NAT, their traffic can push the IP over the short window bucket. We see this a lot in coworking spaces.

maria: How do I enable the dev-proxy? Is there a quick command?

ops: Run this on your machine: 
```
git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/dev-proxy.git
cd dev-proxy
./dev-proxy --mode local --key $SANDBOX_KEY --keepalive
```
It will proxy and multiplex streams, which reduces per-connection throttles.

maria: Great. If I need more sustained throughput for a demo next week, what's the process for a temporary hosted increase?

ops: Open a ticket in #support with: expected tokens/sec, duration, whether streaming or batch, and the root cause (demo/test). Tag me (ops). We can grant a time-limited bump.

devx: If you do open a ticket include a small repro and your client logs (showing the 429s). If Retry-After is missing, sometimes it's the per-second micro-bucket and not the larger quota bucket. In those cases retries with exponential backoff + jitter are recommended.

maria: Any concrete retry recipe?

devx: Simple pattern: start with 200-400ms base, double up to ~8s, add jitter. Pseudo: 
```
wait = base * (2 ** tries) + random(0, base)
```
Also limit overall retries to avoid long hangs in dev.

infra-bot: [system] Note: Key mixing detected in traffic: hosted and sandbox keys used from the same IP 2023-11-08T15:02:10Z. This can cause unexpected throttling.

maria: Oh, that might be my issue 94 I had a curl using hosted and my app using sandbox. I'll switch them.

andy: If you still see flakiness after proxy and clean keys ping me and I can spin up a devbox in the same VPC for you to test from.

maria: Thanks everyone, will try the proxy + keepalive and open a ticket if needed. Appreciate the quick help :heart:
